**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [NO]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

**Synopsis:**
European markets enter autumn under significant stress: benchmark gas prices at 3.5-year highs amid Iran war supply disruptions to Qatari LNG, European stocks at record seasonal lows, and bond markets in sharp sell-off with Bund and OAT futures at multi-year lows. French and German yields hit 15-year highs. Euro zone CPI data due imminently is expected to cement expectations for an ECB rate hike. Globally, US 10-year Treasury yields hit a 20-month high, Japan's 10-year touched 3% for the first time since 1996, and equities fell across Asia. Rising term premia — NY Fed measure shows 10-year Treasury term premium tripled from ~26bps (Jan 2025) to 80bps+ (June) — alongside rising real yields are driving the bond selloff. Trump threatened further Iran strikes, adding geopolitical risk.

**Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?**
Relevance: YES — 10-year Treasury yields hitting a 20-month high, rising term premia, breakeven inflation data, and upcoming US JOLTS/ISM data are all directly referenced.

*(Rising yields, elevated term premium, sticky real yields, and hawkish macro backdrop all point toward sustained upward rate pressure, though the article stops short of explicitly forecasting a Fed hike.)*

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Sentiment: +65 (Hawkish)
*The combination of 20-month high Treasury yields, a tripling of term premia, rising real yields, geopolitical escalation (Iran), and hot inflation data pending all point to a decidedly hawkish tilt. There is no dovish signal present in the article. The dominant narrative is upward yield pressure with no near-term relief catalyst identified.*
